So it aged well.

As discussed earlier, China was the biggest US proxy in Asia until Xi came to power and that Xi will change his behaviour toward the US in the coming time.

Today's statement from Xi where he told Trump that "US and China should be partner, rather than rivals" shows exactly that change in attitude. What remains to be seen is whether the US will change its policy toward China in response. But this statement from Xi is not just a diplomatic sweet line. It reveals the pressure Xi is actually facing right now.

1. Xi played his cards too early. China was not ready to confront the US and is now paying the price.

2. China's entire periphery has been destabilised and flipped to pro-US regimes starting from 2021. 

3. China's eastern front has been militarised with Japan rearming for the first time since WW2, Taiwan's military upgraded with American weapons and military agreements signed with Philippines, Singapore and Indonesia. 

4. The US cut China's rare earth and semiconductor autonomy through the Pax Silica programme and ASML export controls. 

5. The major cheap energy supply lanes China depended on were targeted through regime change in Venezuela, and although the Iran regime change failed, the US inflicted $300-400 billion dollars worth of destruction on Iran, one of China's cheapest energy suppliers. 

6. Chinese weapons have failed publicly and visibly in multiple conflicts since last year, the India-Pakistan war, the Thailand-Cambodia war, the Iran-Israel war, the Venezuela coup and the US-Iran war. Chinese military technology has been exposed as a second hand cheap copy of stolen American military technology. As I said earlier, the only Chinese systems that genuinely perform are their satellites. Everything else underperforms against Chinese claims. China compensates through mass production because cheap cost and high speed manufacturing is what China is actually a master of, not genuine military innovation.

7. China has not fought a real war since 1979 when they lost to Vietnam. Today there is not a single senior officer in the Chinese military with actual battle experience. China has become a business minded country at it's core that has grown its economy to 20 trillion dollars but never grew the resolve that comes from genuine military experience under fire.

Now on the White House statement that China has agreed that Iran should not have nuclear weapons and Politico's report that China put pressure on Iran to have a deal with the US. That is an expected thing and exactly why I said during the Iran war that Iran should not rely on China for security guarantees. Russia is the only credible security guarantor for Iran against a future US-Israel attack. China always prioritises its economic relationship with the US over any ideological commitment to its partners. Today's Xi statement proves that completely.

Now coming to India. If US-China relations improve and the US changes its approach toward China after today's Xi request, India will feel pressure from all sides simultaneously. Both borders will become active in that scenario. A US-China rapprochement is actually the most dangerous geopolitical development for India because it removes the natural tension between our two primary adversaries that has been giving India breathing room.

And finally, the Chinese propaganda spread for years on social media that India is the weakest link and a US vassal in BRICS has been exposed today by Xi's own statement. Because India did not even go to the US to improve relations after the US sanctions for developing nuclear weapons. It was the US that approached India to remove the sanctions and improve relations.

After all, China and Pakistan have only truly mastered one thing across decades. How to run propaganda and how to control narrative through that propaganda.

quoted_tweet.text:
BRICS PARADOX AND INDIA-RUSSIA EQUATION! 

This is the propaganda sold by China that India is the weakest link in BRICS.
The reality is China has always been the secret sidekick of the US. Most of the Chinese establishment is still pro-US, only Xi is an anti-US figure.

US-China relations were great before Xi rose to power in 2012. The €!A was grooming Li Keqiang as the successor of Hu Jintao, but Xi came out of syllabus. US-China relations started deteriorating because Xi wants to be the next Mao of China. In reality, it was China who saved the US empire from collapse during the 2008 financial crisis by rejecting Russia's offer to jointly collapse the US empire. China chose the US and saved it because it was their biggest market and they held enormous amounts of US treasuries. Russia never forgot that Chinese deception to this day. The US being China's biggest market and China being the biggest buyer of US debt is still largely the case. They have dumped some treasuries but it is temporary. If Xi is gone, China's stance will completely change. And in the coming time you will see Xi himself changing his stance toward the US.

Now coming to BRICS, which is an organisation with immense potential but no clear path, because it is stuck in its own paradox. It has been divided into three groups for the last few years. First, China, which wants BRICS to declare the Yuan as a BRICS currency because it wants to replace US hegemony with Chinese hegemony through BRICS. Second, Russia and India, who do not want to be junior partners of China and want a BRICS currency in which every member has an equal share, because both understand that whoever controls the currency controls the group. Third, South Africa and Brazil, who are watching this game from the sidelines and have decided they will side with whoever wins.

China-Russia relations are not as good as they appear on the surface, and India-Russia relations are not as bad as Western media projects them. In reality, India-Russia relations are deeper than Russia-China relations.

But global media will always show that Russia-China relations are strengthening and becoming a threat, while India-US relations are great and India is a US vassal. In reality, China-Russia relations started improving after Xi rose to power because Moscow had turned anti-West by 2012 and saw Xi as a leader who wanted to pull down US hegemony. After the Ukraine war started, China became a necessity for Russia, but that does not mean Russia is becoming a Chinese vassal. Both Russia and China are using each other. Russia is using China to keep its economy alive and China is using Russia to keep the West engaged so it cannot focus on containing China.

In reality, both the US and China want to divide Russia and India, because both understand that a Russia-India partnership has immense possibilities. Russia has the land, the natural resources, and the advanced military technology. India has the population, the human capital, and the market demand. Together they could create a union with a self-sufficient economic space of nearly 1.8 billion people, with enough military power to deter both the US and China, and access to everything from Siberian gas to Indian software. In this scenario Russia could help India become a self-sufficient and sanction immune economy, with military indigenisation as well.

So China and the US will keep pushing the propaganda that India is a US vassal and the weakest link in BRICS, because both fear that a Russia-India strategic partnership can build a pole that neither the US nor China can challenge.

Senior defense reporter Manny Mogato agrees with Senator Trillanes. The footage taken by @ABSCBNNews and other agencies showing the restraint of the NBI agents present corroborates this too, along with the statements from the Armed Forces of the Philippines' Chief of Staff, Gen. Brawner. It's also what Pres. Marcos himself said.

The shots were fired by security staff from either the Sergeant-at-Arms office or private security of a senator. The security services surrounding the Senate stormed in, reacting to the gunfire.

The question now is, who among the senate staff fired, how many of them fired, and why did they fire? What's with all the long-firearms carried by senate security staff at that moment? Why was Sen. Dela Rosa allowed to leave the Senate premises by the staff there and why wasn't he caught by the police cordon around the Senate.

So many questions and I'm tempted to believe Trillanes as he's been right about most things so far, from the Duterte's hidden wealth to the fake war on drugs to the ICC arrest warrants.

Did senators, after hiding an international fugitive, decide to help him evade justice? Isn't that a criminal offence?
